description: Somos COSMIX, un equipo de Cochabamba con curiosidad por descubrir las historias que esconden los datos de nuestro planeta. Queremos explorar datos de la NASA, detectar tendencias y convertirlas en visualizaciones claras y creativas. Buscamos personas con interés en programación, análisis de datos, ciencias de la Tierra, diseño y comunicación. ¡Si te apasiona aprender, colaborar y comprender nuestro mundo, únete a la misión! 🚀
summary: CochaViva turns NASA Earth observations into an exploratory dashboard for Cochabamba’s fifteen districts. Users compare surface temperature and vegetation across September-start composites from 2010–2025, inspect coverage and missing observations, explore a transparent index with adjustable weights, and export results with sources. We calculate robust slopes, confidence intervals and corrected significance tests. Neither analysis window produced significant trends after correction; this does not prove absence of change. A key finding is that Terra’s earlier morning observations can confound apparent temperature trends. CochaViva preserves observation time and a 2010–2020 comparison window instead of treating every decline as climate improvement. The prototype connects reproducible science with local questions for residents and planners, while keeping reference boundaries, fixed 2026 transport context and uncertainty visible.
details:
CochaViva is an exploratory web dashboard that connects NASA Earth observations with questions about the fifteen districts of Cochabamba. It allows users to investigate environmental differences, observe how they evolve, and review the evidence behind each result.

HOW IT WORKS AND BENEFITS

Users select a district, year, and variable on an interactive map; view surface temperature and vegetation time series; compare two districts; adjust the weights of a transparent index; examine its sensitivity; and download results and fact sheets for local review. NASA GIBS provides contextual imagery. Calculations are performed using numerical scientific data, not by interpreting the colors of a satellite photograph.

The intended benefit is to help residents and planners understand the data, formulate questions, and trace a result back to its source. The tool facilitates an informed conversation or a field review; municipal adoption, improvements in decision-making, or policy impacts have not yet been demonstrated.

NASA DATA AND METHOD

We used MODIS Terra MOD11A2 daytime surface temperature and MOD13Q1 NDVI vegetation data. Twenty-nine data points were obtained from the NASA ORNL DAAC TESViS REST service. Three NDVI subsets, corresponding to 2010, 2011, and 2014, come from the NASA Microsoft Planetary Computer data mirror. The originals, query parameters, dates, and SHA-256 hashes are preserved. The mirror identifies collection 061; the ORNL responses do not themselves certify the original HDF collection.

The dataset covers 2010–2025, with 32 source entries and 1,440 composition/district records. There are 479 valid district–year–variable aggregates out of 480. The temperature for District 2 in 2014 remains missing. We do not replace missing values with zero or with fabricated observations. These are compositions whose nominal start date falls in September; they are not exact annual or monthly averages.

We applied quality indicators, pixel-polygon intersection, and valid-area weighting. Trends use the Theil–Sen slope, individual confidence intervals, Kendall’s tests, and Benjamini–Hochberg correction, with at least eight valid years. Neither the full time window nor the 2010–2020 comparison shows significant trends after adjustment to a p-value of less than 0.05. This does not prove the absence of environmental change.

CREATIVE CONTRIBUTION: ALSO INVESTIGATE HOW OBSERVATIONS ARE MADE

A distinctive feature of the project is the recognition that both the environment and the method of observation can change. Earth passes by progressively earlier in the morning. In District 1, the average local solar time of the accepted temperature datasets shifts from 10.325 in 2015 to approximately 9.082 in 2025. Since the surface temperature changes throughout the day, an observed decrease may reflect a combination of environmental variation and changes in the satellite’s schedule. We retain this analysis and a period of comparison. We do not attribute the entire decline to drift, nor do we claim that climate cooling has been proven.

LOCAL CONTEXT AND INDEX

The reference boundaries are sourced from Ciudatos Lab using the 2026-10 Household distribution, under ODbL 1.0; they are not boundaries certified by GAMC. The transportation geometry comes from a file published by GAMC. Geometries are deduplicated, and a distinct network length is calculated for each district. Transportation represents a fixed context as of 2026, not a reconstruction of historical services.

The index initially combines 70% environmental factors and 30% transportation factors. Temperature and NDVI initially account for equal shares of the environmental component. The weights are adjustable, and the normalization references remain fixed across years within this version. This is a partial and normative index, not an official measure of quality of life. Transportation density does not indicate frequency, effective accessibility, or well-being.

TECHNOLOGY AND TESTING

The interface uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Leaflet. Processing uses Python and scientific and geospatial libraries, such as NumPy, SciPy, Shapely, and pyproj. Twenty-seven JavaScript tests and 16 Python tests were passed. These tests ensure technical consistency; they do not constitute independent scientific validation. Our own code is licensed under the MIT License; external resources retain their original terms.

USE OF AI / DISCLOSURE

OpenAI Codex assisted with research, comparison and selection of challenges, conceptual framing, programming, processing, testing, documentation, and production of the demo. We do not claim that the ideation was exclusively human. NASA observations and geometries come from the cited sources; they were not generated by AI. Synthetic test data is separate from the observed dataset. The 30-second demo uses real footage, explanatory text in English, and original music synthesized using AI-assisted code; it includes a visible watermark and metadata. The application does not contain an AI API. AI assistance does not constitute scientific validation.

LIMITATIONS AND NEXT STEPS

We consider seasonality, cloud cover, temporal dependence, quality, coverage, spatial resolution, reference geometries, and observation times. LST is not air temperature; NDVI is not a percentage of trees. The nominal resolutions of 1 km and 250 m do not allow for conclusions at the street level. Comprehensive inventories of parks, schools, and healthcare facilities are lacking; the transportation dataset does not explicitly grant a redistribution license and requires clarification. The next steps include user testing, official boundaries, and independent verification of the effect of satellite timing.
